requirements.statement: Creating a topic and first post preserves author identity, first/last post references, forum last post and topic/post counts.
Replies update topic/forum last post and counts while keeping the first post; editing preserves content and author semantics.
Saved author, first/last post references and counters survive Session refresh and reload from the database.
Hiding and restoring posts or topics maintains the existing user/topic/forum counts and last-post behavior.
Hidden Topic and Post objects are excluded from default queries and remain retrievable through explicit with_hidden() queries.
Establishing Forum, Topic, Post, User and Group relationships must not prematurely autoflush incomplete objects.
Initial topic/post creation invokes each applicable before/after save hook once, on the same object, in its existing order, with correct is_new.
Replies and edits preserve applicable post/topic before/after save hooks, object identity, invocation count, existing order and correct is_new.
Legal object changes made by before-save plugins survive persistence.

Migrate SQLAlchemy 1.3.24 to pinned 1.4.21 in the fixed Python 3.9/SQLite environment; preserve native ORM persistence and modify only the six allowed Python files, leaving checks, locks and environment unchanged.
